card.name: Oaths and swearing-in language
card.fires_on: Words in or right after an oath: "Oath", "sworn", "swore", and the "of" or "affirmation" that follows "oath". Also partway through "affidavits". Seen in legal, historical and news text.

modes.label: Oath wording
modes.description: The word oath, or the words that follow it, such as "of" or "or affirmation".
modes.example: He would take an oath<< of>> allegiance and become a citizen.

modes.label: Sworn in
modes.description: Forms of swear used for taking office or pledging service.
modes.example: Ousted IRS chief Steven Miller is<< sworn>> in on Capitol Hill Friday.

modes.label: Legal sworn documents
modes.description: Partway through affidavit or a similar sworn-statement term.

card.writes: It makes oath and swear words, such as oath, sworn, swore and affidavit, more likely to come next.
card.plain: It lights up on oaths and swearing-in, such as taking an oath of office or signing an affidavit.
